title.narrative: Integrated Food Security and WASH Intervention to Enhance Community Resilience in As-Safira and Qabtan EL Jabal, Aleppo Governorate and Duma, Rural Damascus (Priority Two)

description.narrative: ltpgtSince 2011, Syria has been engulfed in a protracted conflict, which has caused extensive damage to critical infrastructure and resulted in widespread poverty, food insecurity, and a resurgence of waterborne diseases. The earthquake in February 2023 further exacerbated the situation, severely impacting public infrastructure related to bread production and WASH services, thereby challenging people's access to essential services, particularly water, sewage, and bread.ltbrgtA substantial reduction in humanitarian assistance funding in 2024 risks further exacerbating the existing needs in underserved areas, such as the As-Safira sub-districts of the Aleppo Governorate. HEKS/EPER seeks to extend additional support to vulnerable households in these regions through a multi-sectoral, needs-based approach. The strategy emphasizes synergies between HEKS/EPER’s portfolio and the Food Security and WASH sectors.ltbrgtThe proposed intervention will prioritize rehabilitating service delivery infrastructure to promote the resilience of vulnerable, underserved communities. HEKS/EPER will leverage its experience in the Food Security and WASH sectors and its knowledge of the local context and needs to rehabilitate public bakeries and improve their production capacities. HEKS/EPER will also rehabilitate water networks to ensure access to potable drinking water in the targeted areas and that the bakeries are connected to a clean water source.ltbrgtIn alignment with the objectives of FAS and WASH sectors, and the HRP, and based on need assessments conducted by HEKS/EPER (Annexes 007, 008, 009, and 010), the proposed interventions aim to achieve several key outcomes:ltbrgt1. Comprehensive rehabilitation of the bakery buildings in Fajdan and Abu Jrin villages in the As-Safira sub-district of Aleppo, including rehabilitation of sewage, washroom and building repair and maintenance, replacing old, non-functional production lines and installing new generators. This initiative aims to significantly improve access to subsidized bread, benefiting up to 51,241 individuals in the catchment areas of these two bakeries. HEKS/EPER conducted this assessment involving local stakeholders and the community, and based on their findings, the total number of targeted beneficiaries in the area is higher than reported in UNOCHA reports. Therefore, HEKS/EPER relies on the updated information obtained during its internal assessment. After the recent change in control, it was found that there's a dire need to install a production line in Duma bakery as per the attached needs assessment. Also, more recently, due to the high increase in returnees after the liberation in western Aleppo, including Qabtan El Jabal, there's a dire need to rehabilitate Qabtan El Jabal bakery and install a production line since there's no functional public bakery there. HEKS EPER will cover the costs of rehabilitation and part of the production line, and will use the savings from this current SHF project to cover the remaining costs of the production line. ltbrgt2. Rehabilitation of the water network in the As-Safira sub-district to serve 15 villages. This project will improve water access for 4,162 individuals relying on expensive and untrusted water trucking.ltbrgtHEKS/EPER will coordinate with MoWR and MoITCP regarding the agreed scope of work, technical design, and validation of the proposed interventions. The project focuses primarily on community-level technical interventions within public sector infrastructure. HEKS/EPER collaborates with community representatives to ensure their needs and concerns are effectively communicated and addressed, fostering a positive and cooperative approach.ltbrgtUpon successful completion of the rehabilitation works, the relevant Ministry will assume responsibility for the continuous operation and maintenance of the rehabilitated infrastructure. This transition to local management ensures long-term sustainability and improved service delivery to the community.ltbrgtlt/pgt
